extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Department of Education funds (postsecondary institutions and other schools), Title IX coordinators, investigators, appeal decisionmakers, institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX grievance and pregnancy standards
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on (1) design and operation of grievance procedures and appeals under Title IX (including required bases for appeal, impartiality, evidence, and scope of Assistant Secretary review) and (2) the definition and scope of 'pregnancy or related conditions' for nondiscrimination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required bases for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department selected three bases for which a recipient must offer an appeal because each basis represents an error that, if left uncorrected by the recipient, indicates that the determination may be inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may offer appeals on additional bases at their discretion, but if they do so they must offer the same appeal bases to both complainant and respondent (e.g., an appeal of severity of sanctions must be available equally to both parties). The Department deleted references to 'the matter' and made other clarifying revisions to §106.46(i)(1)(i)-(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker independence for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal decisionmaker must not have taken part in an investigation of the allegations or the dismissal of the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement (from §106.45(d)(3)(iii) and incorporated into §106.46(a)) ensures the appeal decisionmaker reviews the underlying case independently and cannot be the same person who investigated or dismissed the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal decisionmaker impartiality and training
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal decisionmaker must be free from bias and conflicts of interest and trained to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See final §106.45(b)(2) (freedom from bias/conflict) and §106.8(d)(2)(iii) (training to serve impartially). The appellate review should account for bias claims where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals not required for simple or clear error
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require that a recipient offer an appeal on the basis of simple error, clear error, or a determination being against the weight of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate cases do not mandate such appeals; however, a determination being against the weight of the evidence can support an inference of bias, and appeals on bias (see §106.46(i)(1)(iii)) can encompass review of outcomes that appear lopsided or erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals may be based on decisionmaker bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may appeal on the basis of decisionmaker bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.46(i)(1)(iii) allows appeals for Title IX Coordinator or investigator bias or conflict of interest. Such appeals can consider whether a decision was against the weight of the evidence as part of an assertion of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: New evidence standard for appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal based on new evidence is limited to evidence that was not reasonably available at the time the determination or dismissal was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.46(i)(1)(ii) already specifies this; it guards against a party inappropriately withholding evidence during the investigation to present it only on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic forfeiture of evidence not presented at investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to deem any evidence not presented during the investigation forfeited during a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because not every recipient will include a live hearing under §106.46, deeming unpresented evidence forfeited could be inapplicable or overly restrictive for many recipients and is therefore not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology must not imply required live hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory wording should avoid implying that a live hearing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to use the word 'adjudication' in place of 'determination' because 'adjudication' might be interpreted as synonymous with 'hearing' and would be inconsistent with §106.46(g) which does not require a live hearing for every recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of Title IX Coordinator/investigator as appealable bias sources
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Title IX Coordinator' and 'investigator' remain in §106.46(i)(1)(iii) to permit appeals based on their bias or conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bias or conflict by these actors may not always amount to a procedural irregularity, but providing the opportunity to appeal on those grounds promotes accuracy in grievance procedures and helps fulfill Title IX's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion in designing grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have flexibility and discretion to design and implement grievance procedures appropriate for their education program or activity, so long as they are consistent with §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are better positioned to know their communities' needs and values. Regardless of structure, procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably under §106.45(b)(1). The Department will provide technical assistance as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance and appeal procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required by §106.45(b)(1); recipients offering additional appeal bases or structuring appeals in any fashion must ensure parity between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Assistant Secretary (OCR) review
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.47 applies only to determinations regarding whether sex-based harassment occurred under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46; OCR will not substitute its judgment for a recipient's decisionmaker regarding weighing of relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR enforces compliance consistent with its authority (20 U.S.C. 1682) and may hold recipients accountable for noncompliance with Title IX regulations; filing a private lawsuit is separate from OCR administrative enforcement and students are not required to notify OCR when filing suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions'—scope
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pregnancy or related conditions' includes pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, and all related medical conditions and recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition covers the full spectrum of processes and events connected with pregnancy; the Department deleted the word 'their' for clarity so recovery reads '[r]ecovery from pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, or related medical conditions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy-related condition need not be an ADA disability
rubrics_metrics.description: A pregnancy-related medical condition does not have to qualify as a disability under the ADA for it to fall within the Title IX definition or to qualify for a reasonable modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 106.10 and 106.40(b)(3)(ii) do not rely on the ADA; if someone also has an ADA/Section 504 disability they are protected under those statutes as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of perceived and potential pregnancy-related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition and Title IX protections extend to discrimination based on perceived pregnancy status and to 'potential' pregnancy or related conditions (i.e., expected, likely, or capacity to occur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers situations such as rumors about fertility care, planning for pregnancy, or expectations that someone may become pregnant. Title IX also prohibits discrimination based on sex stereotypes and expectations about pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exhaustive list of pregnancy-related medical conditions in regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not add a list of specific medical conditions to the regulatory text to avoid confusion or implying exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble nonetheless provides examples (not exhaustive) including pregnancy-related fatigue, dehydration, nausea, anemia, bladder dysfunction, gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, hyperemesis gravidarum, pregnancy-induced hypertension, infertility, recovery from childbirth/miscarriage/abortion, ectopic pregnancy, prenatal/postpartum depression, and lactation conditions such as swelling, leaking, or mastitis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of 'termination of pregnancy' and its meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'termination of pregnancy' is included and interpreted to mean the end of pregnancy in any manner, including miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion; it also includes medical conditions related to and recovery from termination of pregnancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX prohibits discrimination based on seeking, obtaining, or having experienced termination of pregnancy, subject only to specific narrow limitations (see section 1688 discussion). The inclusion simply incorporates longstanding regulatory text since 1975.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of 20 U.S.C. 1688 (Danforth Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1688 limits the Department's enforcement by providing that Title IX 'shall not be construed to require or prohibit any person ... to provide or pay for any benefit or service, including the use of facilities, related to an abortion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of section 1688, Title IX does not require a recipient (e.g., campus health center or student insurance plan) to provide or pay for abortions. But section 1688 does not allow recipients to impose penalties on persons for seeking or having had a legal abortion when the penalty is unrelated to providing such benefits; targeting individuals for adverse treatment because they obtained abortion care may still violate section 1681. Inquiries into the circumstances of an abortion may be discriminatory, and recipients can usually implement protections without asking specifics about an abortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with Dobbs and state laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Dobbs decision does not alter the Department's interpretation of 'pregnancy or related conditions,' 'termination of pregnancy,' or Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate; inclusion of termination of pregnancy in Title IX protections is not a response to Dobbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about how Title IX protections interact with State abortion restrictions should be evaluated case-by-case; the Department will offer technical assistance as appropriate. Policies that specifically target individuals who received abortion care may violate section 1681 regardless of state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for regulating pregnancy-related discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department asserts that regulating discrimination based on pregnancy or related conditions, including termination of pregnancy, falls within its Title IX authority and does not raise major questions doctrine concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites Congress' express delegation to issue regulations prohibiting sex discrimination under Title IX (20 U.S.C. 1682) and relevant Supreme Court precedent (e.g., Gebser).
